subject: Priority: Dedicated headroom alarm — Summit Retail throughput breach
messages:
From: Alex Chu <alex.chu@summitretail.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, support@redwood.com
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@summitretail.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Production errors & latency spike — Summit Retail (Prod)

Hi Sean / Redwood Support team,

We started seeing increased 5xx errors and a large P95 latency jump on our production inference route (model: rdx/large-v2) around 08:02 PDT. Errors are primarily 503s and timeouts; our dashboard shows sustained queueing and requests throttled despite our reserved capacity.

Impact: checkout conversion is affected (~8% revenue drop in the last 10 minutes). This is high severity for us — please advise immediate mitigations. I attached a short error dump and a brief metrics snapshot.

Attachments: summit-error-sample.log, summit-metrics-snapshot.csv

Thanks,
Alex Chu
Head of Engineering, Summit Retail
alex.chu@summitretail.com

---
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chu <alex.chu@summitretail.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@summitretail.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors & latency spike — Summit Retail (Prod)

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. I’m escalating internally now. Our initial read is consistent with dedicated GPU pool pressure that’s impacting reserved throughput for your slots.

Immediate actions we’re initiating:
- Ops will triage pool utilization and attempt a quick reroute to a compatible model variant where possible.
- I’ve asked for a temporary burst authorization while we stabilize (we’ll pursue formal approval in parallel).
- We’ll provision an ops bridge at T+15 for live triage if the customer prefers.

Can you confirm if any heavy batch jobs or a deploy started around 07:45–08:00? That info helps narrow root cause.

I’ll keep you updated every 15 minutes until we have a stable state. Apologies for the disruption — we know this is critical.

Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0189

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chu <alex.chu@summitretail.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@summitretail.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors & latency spike — Summit Retail (Prod)

Sean / team — quick ops triage summary (preliminary):
- Observed sustained GPU util ~98% on dedicated-pool-7 (zone: us-west-2).
- Reserved throughput for Summit Retail has diverged ~-35% versus committed QPS for the 08:00–08:30 window.
- Kernel-level contention + KV-cache churn for long-context requests correlates with the latency tail.
- Error wave is largely 503s (queue-full) and a small subset of gRPC timeouts (10s).

Immediate remediation steps applied:
1) Enabled automatic fallback to model-variant rdx/medium-v2 for non-critical routes (rate-limited) — cut P95 in the test slice from ~820ms -> ~260ms.
2) Initiated slow-roll traffic reroute for 25% of traffic to a less saturated pool (will monitor).
3) Requesting burst unlock (temporary capacity +20%) while engineering investigates root cause.

I’ve attached the ops quickpatch runbook we used. If we get exec signoff for burst authorization we can push an additional 30% headroom within 5–7 minutes.

Attachments: ops-runbook-quickpatch.pdf

Follow-ups for engineering: please dump kernel logs for pool-7 and check recent orchestration decisions (could be noisy neighbor or cross-tenant spillover).

—Olga
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chu <alex.chu@summitretail.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@summitretail.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors & latency spike — Summit Retail (Prod)

Alex / Samira — I’m very sorry for the disruption. We recognize checkout is high impact and appreciate the quick report.

Immediate customer-facing commitments:
- We’re offering a temporary 72-hour service credit for the window of impact; we’ll follow up with a formal credit amount after post-incident analysis.
- We will prioritize burst capacity for Summit Retail while ops stabilizes the pool. I’ve started the internal approval thread for a temporary capacity increase; I’ll own the customer communication.
- Offer: 30-minute ops + product sync after this stabilizes to walk through root cause and mitigation (we’ll schedule at your convenience).

Alex — please let me know if you want the ops bridge now or prefer updates in this thread. We will not close the ticket until your production latencies are back in normal range.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors & latency spike — Summit Retail (Prod)

Team — summary and ask for exec/billing signoff:

Summary of current state:
- Customer: Summit Retail (deal DL-4872). Impacting prod checkout — visible revenue loss.
- Cause (prelim): Dedicated GPU pool saturation (dedicated-pool-7) with reserved-throughput shortfall (-35%). Ops has applied a partial reroute and fallback; P95 improved on the test slice but the overall reservation is still below commitment.
- Actions taken: partial traffic reroute, fallback variant enabled, ops quickpatch applied. We can unlock temporary burst capacity (target +20–30%) within minutes if billing/exec signoff is provided.

Ask: Marcus / Priyom — please approve temporary burst and a goodwill credit (72 hours) to be applied to Summit Retail’s account while we complete RCA. Legal/procurement may need to be looped for contract language impacting reserved guarantees. If you approve, Olga can enact the additional capacity immediately and I’ll notify the customer.

If anyone prefers a live bridge, I’ll set that up now (Ops + CS + Summit Eng).

Thanks — standing by for approval.

Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
